title: macOS: every mouse button press suppresses mouse motion events for 150-250 ms
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.6.1.stable.mono (official, 14d19694e).

### System information

macOS 26.6.2 (25G83), Apple M1 Max, Forward+ / Metal

### Issue description

On macOS, every mouse button press stops `InputEventMouseMotion` delivery for roughly 150 to 250 ms. The motion is not lost: it is withheld and then delivered as two or three very large events. In a first person camera this reads as the view freezing on each click and then snapping, which makes aiming while firing unusable.

It happens in both `MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED` and `MOUSE_MODE_CONFINED_HIDDEN`, with `Input.use_accumulated_input` set to false, and it is unrelated to frame rate. It does not happen in a plain AppKit window on the same machine in the same session, which suggests the cause is in the macOS platform input path rather than in the OS itself.

Measured in a project instrumented to timestamp every input event on one `Time.get_ticks_usec()` clock:

| | duration | motion events | clicks | gaps over 100 ms | median gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Godot, clicking | 26.8 s | 65.1/s | 1.7/s | 1.9/s | 147 ms |
| Godot, panning without clicking | 15.7 s | 75.0/s | 0 | 0.4/s | 408 ms, stdev 767 ms |
| Plain AppKit window, clicking | 20.8 s | 109.8/s | 2.8/s | 0.05/s | one gap, 1.2 s from any click |

The number of blackouts tracks the click rate one for one. Without clicking, the remaining gaps are few and have a large spread, consistent with a hand pausing rather than a fixed interval. With clicking, the gap length is tightly clustered, which points at a timer rather than at user behaviour.

In a larger project the clustering is tighter still: 24 blackouts over 10.1 s at a median of 248.3 ms with a standard deviation of 9.4 ms, against 2.4 clicks per second. 0.25 s is the default `LocalEventsSuppressionInterval` on macOS, the window during which the system discards real input after a process posts a synthetic event.

`warp_mouse()` in `platform/macos/display_server_macos.mm` already sets that interval to zero on a newly created event source and calls `CGAssociateMouseAndMouseCursorPosition(true)` after warping, but the event source it configures is not the one the warp uses, so the suppression may still apply. `windowDidBecomeKey:` in `platform/macos/godot_window_delegate.mm` also warps, though only under `MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED`, and the problem occurs in confined mode as well, where that path does not run.

The button event itself appears to be delayed along with the motion, so a naive log timestamps the click at the end of the blackout rather than at its start.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the attached project on macOS and run it.
2. Move the mouse continuously and click the left button about once a second for 15 seconds.
3. Press Escape to quit and read the summary printed to the console.

Expect the gaps between motion events to stay small. Observed is roughly one gap over 100 ms per click.

The whole project is one script:

```gdscript
extends Node

var motion_times: Array[int] = []
var click_times: Array[int] = []
var label: Label

func _ready() -> void:
	Input.use_accumulated_input = false
	Input.mouse_mode = Input.MOUSE_MODE_CAPTURED
	label = Label.new()
	label.position = Vector2(20, 20)
	add_child(label)

func _input(event: InputEvent) -> void:
	if event is InputEventMouseMotion:
		motion_times.append(Time.get_ticks_usec())
	elif event is InputEventMouseButton and event.pressed:
		if event.button_index == MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT:
			click_times.append(Time.get_ticks_usec())
	elif event is InputEventKey and event.pressed and event.keycode == KEY_ESCAPE:
		get_tree().quit()

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
	label.text = "pan continuously and click about once a second\nEsc to finish\nmotion %d   clicks %d" % [motion_times.size(), click_times.size()]

func _exit_tree() -> void:
	if motion_times.size() < 2:
		print("not enough motion recorded")
		return
	var gaps: Array[float] = []
	for i in range(1, motion_times.size()):
		gaps.append((motion_times[i] - motion_times[i - 1]) / 1000.0)
	var blackouts: Array[float] = []
	for g in gaps:
		if g > 100.0:
			blackouts.append(g)
	var span := (motion_times[-1] - motion_times[0]) / 1000000.0
	print("duration %.1f s" % span)
	print("motion events %d  (%.1f/s)" % [motion_times.size(), motion_times.size() / span])
	print("clicks %d  (%.1f/s)" % [click_times.size(), click_times.size() / span])
	print("gaps over 100 ms: %d  (%.1f/s)" % [blackouts.size(), blackouts.size() / span])
	blackouts.sort()
	if blackouts.size() > 0:
		print("median gap %.1f ms   min %.1f   max %.1f" % [blackouts[blackouts.size() / 2], blackouts[0], blackouts[-1]])
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

The script above is the entire project. Attach it to a single `Node` in the main scene of an empty project.

For comparison, the AppKit control used above is a plain window that logs `mouseMoved`, `mouseDragged` and `mouseDown` timestamps, with no capture and no warping. It shows continuous motion delivery through 58 clicks on the same machine.
